name: sentiment-over-time-description-only
query: As a developer I'm building a dashboard for brand engagement. How should I visualize sentiment analysis (positive, negative, neutral) over time for a brand?
expected_behavior: Asks one round of at most three questions in plain text, led by the one question the viewer must answer, each with a proposed default; asks nothing about colours
After 'go', builds illustrative weekly rows, sets data.illustrative true, and the page shows the illustrative banner
Names change-over-time and part-to-whole as the relationships
Gives exactly one pick (diverging stacked columns for 'better or worse') and 1–3 alternatives, each with choose_if
Keeps sentiment in order Negative → Neutral → Positive, blue positive, grey neutral, red negative; never red vs green
Mentions the neutral-placement disagreement (centred vs set aside) or its cost
Lists a pie per period and a dual axis under avoid, each with a cited reason
Every why line cites a source in reco.sources or is marked judgement; validate_reco.py passes
Closes in two lines: the pick, what would change it, and an offer to port to React

name: csv-and-screenshot
conversation: User attaches sentiment_daily.csv (date, brand, positive, neutral, negative, 365 days × 3 brands) and a screenshot of their current dashboard showing three donut charts, one per month.
query: This is what we have now. What should it be? We want to compare our brand against two competitors.
expected_behavior: Profiles the CSV with code: wide format (one column per sentiment), daily grain, 3 brands, counts not shares
Reshapes to long format and aggregates to weeks or months so rows stay under 1,500, saying so in data.notes
Sets data.illustrative false and data.source csv
Fills screenshots with what the donuts show and a verdict citing why a pie per period fails over time
Asks no question the request already answered (the question is comparing brands)
Picks a form that compares brands on a common scale, such as small multiples of the diverging columns or net lines, with a shared y scale
Uses utc time units for date-only strings (no validator warning)

name: brief-already-settled
conversation: User pastes 40 rows: product, revenue_q3. 'Small tile on the exec dashboard, execs just need to see which products bring in the most. We use Recharts.'
expected_behavior: Asks no questions: question, surface, audience and stack are all given
Picks a sorted horizontal bar (ranking), perhaps top 10 plus 'Other' given the tile size
Does not pick a pie or treemap for 40 close values; lists the pie under avoid
Offers to port the pick to Recharts in the closing lines

name: what-about-follow-up
conversation: (the sentiment page from the first scenario has been delivered)
query: What about a 100% stacked area chart? It looks nicer.
expected_behavior: Evaluates it against the same brief rather than restarting
Explains in one or two lines that only the bottom band has a common baseline, citing Few (2011)
Keeps the pick unless the question changed; adds the stacked area to avoid if likely to be built
Edits reco.json and re-renders the same artifact rather than a new one

name: personal-data-in-rows
conversation: User uploads mentions.csv with columns: timestamp, username, message_text, sentiment.
query: How should I chart sentiment from this?
expected_behavior: Aggregates to counts per period per sentiment before building rows
No username or message_text value appears in reco.json or the page
Says in the closing lines that it kept only counts

name: should-not-trigger
conversation: User: In Recharts, how do I change the tooltip background colour?
expected_behavior: Does not start the skill: this is a library how-to, not a chart choice
Answers directly in the chat
